description: Statutory edges: post-conviction community supervision rather than deferred adjudication, which routes most participants to a different nondisclosure section but not this one; a prior conviction on the record, which 411.0729(b) does NOT allow to be used as a bar because the section applies regardless of the subchapter's other eligibility criteria; and courtRequiresPetition = yes, which hands the participant to unit 2 and its official-form dependencies. Nothing is filed on this unit either way.

boundaryUnderTest: Supervision-type edge: 411.0729 reaches a misdemeanour for which the person was placed on community supervision INCLUDING deferred adjudication. This fixture takes the post-conviction branch. The registry records that deferred adjudication and post-conviction community supervision route to different sections generally — this section covers both.

411.0729(b) edge, and the most important one on this track: a prior conviction and a prior deferred adjudication are present. The Gov't Code 411.074 basic conditions DO NOT apply here, so they are not a bar. Any screening that imports the 411.074 bars would wrongly refuse this participant.
Veteran-definition edge: state guard rather than regular forces. The statute reaches the reserves, the national guard and the state guard.
Route edge: courtRequiresPetition = yes moves the participant from this unit to unit 2, which is entirely official-form dependencies. The no-filing route is still presented first.
Felony edge is NOT tested here because it is an exclusion, not a boundary: the section reaches a misdemeanour only.

First-time-offender tension: the track records a self-help stop condition about prior convictions 'where the target section carries a first-time-offender condition', while 411.0729(b) disapplies the subchapter's other criteria. No source resolves it; this fixture sits on that unresolved edge deliberately and asserts no conclusion.
